capabilities.problem: A confident financial answer is useless when I cannot tell which source, statement, or correction produced it.
capabilities.summary: Ledgerglass keeps immutable account and transaction observations, statement facts, corrections, and derived explanations separate so an agent can show its work without trusting a mutable source cache.
capabilities.title: Evidence before answers

capabilities.problem: Floating-point totals and mixed currencies can make a tidy dashboard mathematically wrong.
capabilities.summary: Arithmetic uses integer minor units and keeps currencies separate unless an explicit conversion exists.
capabilities.title: Money that adds up

capabilities.problem: Late settlement, exclusive date boundaries, and provider limits make a naive daily fetch lose rows.
capabilities.summary: The connector uses bounded windows, inclusive human dates, an exclusive API boundary, and overlapping incremental reads.
capabilities.title: Boring, bounded synchronization

capabilities.problem: Some providers stop reporting pending purchases without saying whether they settled or disappeared.
capabilities.summary: Old pending rows can expire from operational totals, return when observed again, or link to a later posted transaction without erasing history.
capabilities.title: Pending is not forever

capabilities.problem: A connected card can still omit posted transactions or report rows that the closed statement does not support.
capabilities.summary: A complete closed statement is matched against the ledger, exact gaps are repaired, uncertain rows stay visible, and later provider evidence can replace overlays.
capabilities.title: Statements can correct the feed

capabilities.problem: Statement gaps, provider differences, conflicting card terms, and repair cases become dangerous when each subsystem keeps its own idea of what is unresolved.
capabilities.summary: Ledgerglass gives closed statement cycles stable identity, preserves field-level fact lineage, proves adjacent-cycle continuity, and routes every unresolved difference through one append-only discrepancy history with deterministic repair postconditions.
capabilities.title: One place for every unresolved difference

capabilities.problem: Spending, debt, transfers, and recurring commitments should not change because a language model phrased them differently.
capabilities.summary: Deterministic read models calculate cashflow, debt, net worth, merchants, transfers, and recurring cadence before narrative is added. Commitment evidence stays separate from interest, fees, debt movement, and repeated discretionary spending; APR buckets are not applied to balances without allocation evidence.
capabilities.title: The totals do not need a model

capabilities.problem: A useful correction should teach the system without silently rewriting old evidence or poisoning evaluation data.
capabilities.summary: Owner corrections and exact statement facts can produce narrow rules with provenance, impact checks, and automatic suspension after contradiction.
capabilities.title: Corrections that can be undone

capabilities.problem: Connecting the tools is not enough if every agent guesses a different workflow or trust policy.
capabilities.summary: Portable skills teach agents how to start, which evidence to prefer, when to ask before writing, and how to qualify incomplete data.
capabilities.title: The same financial habits in every agent

capabilities.problem: Indexes, enrichment, briefings, and derived views fail independently and should not wait for me to notice.
capabilities.summary: A durable agent coordinates bounded retries and cases while the ledger remains the source of financial truth.
capabilities.title: A steward for the boring repair work

capabilities.problem: An unfamiliar merchant may need the web, but the web does not need my account or transaction identifiers.
capabilities.summary: Only a sanitized merchant signal leaves the ledger, and researched claims remain derived evidence rather than transaction truth.
capabilities.title: Research without leaking the ledger

capabilities.problem: Different finance tasks have different latency, structure, and failure needs.
capabilities.summary: The private deployment uses task-specific routing and fallbacks; the public package explains a provider-neutral boundary instead of publishing personal quotas or credentials.
capabilities.title: Model routing from a real deployment

capabilities.problem: The owner needs a visual way to inspect evidence and authorize existing ledger operations without creating a second financial backend.
capabilities.summary: The private deployment has an authenticated console over the same finance application services, with typed evidence workflows, read-only review queues, revision-bound previews, and a separate assistant that can cite evidence or prepare a draft but cannot apply it. Only the architectural and authority boundary is documented publicly.
capabilities.title: A private operator console
